content: 1. For the Sunday starter regimen of norgestimate/ethinyl estradiol, take one hormonally active tablet daily for 21 days, followed by one inert tablet daily for 7 days. This cycle is repeated. Begin the regimen on the Sunday following the onset of menstruation. If menstruation begins on a Sunday, start the regimen on that same day. Use an additional method of contraception during the first 7 days of consecutive administration. 2. For the Day 1 starter regimen, take the first dose on the first day of the menstrual cycle and continue taking one tablet daily. 3. For the 21-tablet package, take one tablet daily for 21 days, followed by 7 days off the medication. 4. For the 28-tablet package, take one tablet daily without interruption. 5. In patients with renal impairment, use with caution and monitor blood pressure. 6. In patients with hepatic impairment, do not administer the medication. 7. Follow the manufacturer’s color-coding for the sequence of administration, especially with triphasic formulations. 8. The safety and efficacy of this medication have not been established in certain populations or conditions. 9. Ethinyl estradiol increases the level or effect of fezolinetant by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. Fezolinetant’s AUC and peak plasma concentration are increased when coadministered with weak, moderate, or strong CYP1A2 inhibitors. 10. Ethinyl estradiol, when coadministered with ombitasvir/paritaprevir/ritonavir and dasabuvir, can lead to significant ALT elevations (>5x ULN, including some >20x ULN). Discontinue ethinyl estradiol-containing medications before initiating hepatitis C combination therapy and restart approximately 2 weeks after completing the regimen. 11. Coadministration of tranexamic acid and ethinyl estradiol increases the risk of thrombosis due to pharmacodynamic synergism. This combination is contraindicated. 12. Amobarbital decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. The efficacy of hormonal contraceptives may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 13. Ethinyl estradiol decreases the effects of anastrozole by pharmacodynamic antagonism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Anastrozole should not be given concurrently with estrogens or estrogen-containing products. 14. Apalutamide decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Apalutamide, a strong CYP3A4 inducer, can lower exposure to CYP3A4 substrates, including ethinyl estradiol. Evaluate for loss of therapeutic effect and adjust doses as needed. 15. Armodafinil decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. The efficacy of hormonal contraceptives may be reduced, and nonhormonal contraception is recommended. 16. Atazanavir may increase or decrease levels of norgestimate by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Use alternatives if available. 17. Ethinyl estradiol increases the level or effect of alprazolam by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Ethinyl estradiol may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation, increasing serum concentrations. 18. Ethinyl estradiol and aminocaproic acid may lead to additive hypercoagulability. Use caution and monitor. Estrogens increase clotting factor production and platelet aggregation, while aminocaproic acid inhibits fibrinolysis and plasminogen activity. 19. Amoxicillin decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. 20. Ampicillin decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. 21. Artemether/lumefantrine decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 22. Ethinyl estradiol increases the level or effect of atogepant by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 23. Atorvastatin increases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor. 24. Ethinyl estradiol increases levels of axitinib by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 25. Ethinyl estradiol increases levels of bendamustine by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Bendamustine is metabolized to minimally active metabolites by CYP1A2, and ethinyl estradiol, a weak CYP1A2 inhibitor, may increase bendamustine plasma concentrations. 26. Ethinyl estradiol increases the level or effect of caffeine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP1A2 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. 27. Carbamazepine decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol and norgestimate by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Advise patients to use alternative contraception during coadministration and for 28 days after discontinuing therapy. 28. Cefaclor decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. 29. Cefadroxil decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. 30. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. An alternative or additional form of birth control may be advisable during concomitant use. 34. Cefixime decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. Cenobamate decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Modify therapy or monitor closely. Advise women to use additional or alternative nonhormonal birth control when using cenobamate with oral contraceptives. 41. Cephalexin decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. 42. Ciprofloxacin decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. 46. Clarithromycin decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but modify therapy or monitor closely. 47. Clindamycin decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol by altering intestinal flora. This applies only to oral forms of the hormone. There is a low risk of contraceptive failure, but caution and monitoring are advised. 48. Clobazam decreases the level or effect of ethinyl estradiol and norgestimate by affecting hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Clobazam is a weak CYP3A4 inducer, and the effectiveness of hormonal contraceptives may be diminished. Additional nonhormonal forms of contraception are recommended. 49. Ethinyl estradiol increases the level or effect of clonazepam by decreasing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor. Ethinyl estradiol may inhibit the clearance of benzodiazepines that undergo oxidation, increasing serum concentrations. 50. Elvitegravir/cobicistat/emtricitabine/tenofovir DF increases norgestimate levels and may result in insulin resistance, dyslipidemia, acne, and venous thrombosis. It decreases ethinyl estradiol levels, potentially reducing efficacy. Modify therapy or monitor closely. 51. Ethinyl estradiol increases levels of cyclosporine by an unknown mechanism. Use caution and monitor.
